inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2-2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares 46.9M (basic on cover 46.36M at 2026-07-15 plus ~0.55M option dilution). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution too would double-count).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K, us-gaap:StockOptionPlanExpense $39.6M (FY2024 $37.7M, FY2023 $32.3M; 9M-2025 quarterly AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $30.7M ties). TDY publishes no separate tax-withholding-on-net-share-settlement line in XBRL and its awards are predominantly options exercised for cash (FY2025 proceeds $48.8M), so the equity-award tax cost is immaterial; no combined figure exists.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending Sunday nearest 31 December (FY2025 ended 2025-12-28)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 (defense/space ballast offsets industrial-instrumentation cyclicality) -> cost of equity ~9.2%. Debt ~6% of capital (net debt $1.69B vs ~$28.7B market cap) at ~4.5% pre-tax / ~3.5% after tax -> WACC ~8.8%, used as 8.75% in every scenario (risk charged once, through the scenarios, not via per-scenario WACC).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (FY2025 lease cost $46.1M, payments $43.7M) sit inside operating income and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment: lease cost in the flows, liabilities out of the bridge. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore zero.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US filer, moderately cyclical diversified industrial/defense electronics). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1/2; adaptations considered but none bind beyond lease consistency and cyclical-cap discipline (USD flows, USD quote, no NCI, SBC non-zero). FY0 = FY2025 (revenue $6,115.4M). Year 1 = FY2026 guidance (raised July 2026 to >$6.53B, +6.8%, includes full-year Excelitas A&D/DD-Scientific acquired revenue). ADJ EBITDA is pre-SBC: FY2025 operating income 1,149.8 + D&A 336.3 + SBC 39.6 = 1,525.7 (24.9%); H1-2026 = 627.4 + 172.9 + 19.5 = 819.8 (25.4%). D&A includes $216.6M of acquired-intangible amortization (3.5% of revenue) which rolls off over the horizon; the D&A path glides from 5.4% to 2.3% so the terminal year does not perpetuate an amortization tax shield (terminal D&A ~ depreciation ~ capex). Cash tax on EBIT: FY2025 cash taxes paid $280.2M / EBIT $1,149.8M = 24.4%, FY2024 21.6%, FY2023 30% (Sec.174 R&D capitalisation); the 2025 OBBBA restoration of domestic R&D expensing lowers near-term cash tax, so the path is 22% in FY2026 rising to 23.5%. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables+inventory > payables, so wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-10% of incremental revenue). BUYBACKS: $402.9M in FY2025, $354.0M FY2024, only $2.9M H1-2026 (capital going to debt paydown and M&A) -- the flat share count is funded intermittently. PENDING VAREX IMAGING ACQUISITION (~$1.1B cash, $18.90/sh, close expected early 2027) is NOT modelled: it is unclosed, debt/cash funded and assumed priced at roughly fair value, so it is value-neutral to a first approximation; on close it adds ~$1.1B to net debt and ~$0.85B of revenue. Unmodelled serial M&A is likewise excluded (its growth is excluded together with its cost). Interest income is not stripped (TDY is net debt). Price is a regular-session close.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Blend of revenue 3yr CAGR (3.9%, post-FLIR organic-plus-bolt-on) and FY2026 guidance (+6.8%), backed by ~$5.0B funded backlog and book-to-bill >1.0 for 11 quarters. Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor: 5yr is inflated by the FLIR share issuance.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 26.6% diverges >30% from revenue (14.6%) and EPS (11.8%) -- driven by ~$4B of stock issued for FLIR in FY2021, not retained earnings. 5yr revenue/EPS CAGRs also embed FLIR and are not organic.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped; net debt). Owner FCF: FY2020 517.5, FY2022 362.7, FY2025 1,034.4. The 3yr FCF CAGR (41.8%) is an artefact of a depressed FY2022 base (tax on divestitures and Sec.174 cash taxes) and is not a growth signal. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (14.9%) is slightly ABOVE reported (14.4%): SBC grew slower than cash flow, so no SBC-funded growth concern.

base.narrative: Guided FY2026 then mid-single-digit growth fading to 3%; modest margin expansion on mix and operating leverage.

bull.narrative: Defense supercycle and space/unmanned/counter-UAS above 10% lift organic growth to high single digits.

bear.narrative: H2-2026 miss, then an industrial/instrumentation downturn plus China export-control losses and a defense budget plateau.

scenario_narratives.base: Teledyne delivers the raised FY2026 outlook (>$6.53B, +6.8% including acquired DD-Scientific and full-year Excelitas A&D), then grows mid-single digits as the ~$5.0B funded backlog and 11 straight quarters of book-to-bill >1.0 convert, with Digital Imaging's space, unmanned and counter-UAS lines (>10% growth) offsetting flat Instrumentation and Engineered Systems. Growth fades to 3% by year 8 as the defense budget step-up normalises. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin edges from 25.4% to 26.5% on mix and FLIR integration leverage, roughly the H1-2026 run-rate plus one point, well inside the 27-28% peers like AMETEK earn. Acquired-intangible amortization rolls off, so the D&A tax shield fades and cash tax settles at ~23.5%. Varex and future bolt-ons are excluded on the view that Teledyne pays fair prices.
scenario_narratives.bull: The proposed ~$1.5T FY2027 US defense budget and allied rearmament make the current order surge (Q2-2026 orders +20%, Digital Imaging book-to-bill 1.4x) a multi-year step-up rather than a spike: FLIR thermal, counter-UAS, space-qualified sensors and unmanned systems drive 7-8.5% organic growth for four years, industrial machine-vision and marine instrumentation recover, and operating leverage plus vertical integration in infrared lift pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 28%. Terminal growth 3% and a 20x cap reflect a durable niche-compounder with qualified/sole-source positions.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 lands short of guidance as H2 industrial demand softens, then the bear axes compound: US export controls and entity-list restrictions cut China (a top-five international market) sales of dual-use thermal and imaging products, tariffs raise semiconductor and optics input costs, Instrumentation and machine-vision follow global industrial capex down, and the defense budget plateaus under continuing resolutions after the 2026-27 surge. Revenue grows only 1-1.5% in years 2-3 and pre-SBC EBITDA margin falls to 23.5% before recovering to 24% -- roughly the FY2022-24 GAAP-equivalent range. Terminal growth 2%, 15x cap for a slower, more cyclical conglomerate. Leadership continuity (Mehrabian's contract expires December 2026) adds execution risk to the M&A machine.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): the stock trades near the top of a defense-spending upcycle with China export-control exposure and an industrial-cyclical half of the portfolio, though leverage is the lowest in six years so there is no solvency tail. Base 50%: guidance has just been raised and is backed by a record funded backlog. Bull 30% (down from 35%): it needs both a sustained defense step-up and an industrial recovery, two largely independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Teledyne is valued as a diversified, moderately cyclical sensor/instrumentation/defense-electronics operating company on strict owner FCF: SBC (small, ~0.65% of revenue) expensed with a flat diluted share count, components built per year rather than carrying the FY2025 FCF margin forward, acquired-intangible amortization allowed to roll off so its tax shield is not perpetuated, and growth limited to the organic business -- pending Varex and future bolt-on M&A are excluded on both sides of the ledger.
key_risks_to_valuation: Serial M&A is the core of the historical growth record; excluding it understates growth if Teledyne keeps buying below intrinsic value, and overstates value if it overpays (Varex ~$1.1B pending).
US export controls on China (top-five international market) for dual-use thermal/imaging products.
Defense/space budget timing: the order surge may be a peak, not a step-up.
Industrial/instrumentation cyclicality in roughly half of revenue.
Terminal value is the majority of EV; WACC +/-1pp moves value materially (see sensitivity grid).
